security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, fixed repository links, marketing terms, and metadata URLs. No reviewed content executes commands, resolves user-controlled traversal paths, performs reconnaissance, or sends network requests. One semantic concern remains: the skill stores sensitive signed terms in durable memory without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Sensitive contract terms are persisted without explicit user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before storing rates or signed terms, minimize retained fields, document retention, and keep creator records access-controlled.

content.value_statement: Influencer agreements can leave deliverables, payment, rights, and exclusivity unclear. This skill drafts structured agreements and reviews incoming terms for gaps and negotiation risks.
actual_capabilities: Collects parties, campaign dates, deliverables, compensation, usage rights, exclusivity, approvals, and platforms.
Drafts an influencer agreement using an adaptable 11-section framework.
Reviews incoming agreements for missing terms, one-sided clauses, and common red flags.
Explains material clauses, their purpose, and practical issues to examine.
Creates negotiation guidance for rights, exclusivity, revisions, approvals, payment, and whitelisting.
limitations: Provides general templates and information, not legal advice.
Requires accurate deal terms and contract text from the user.
Does not verify enforceability, governing law, or jurisdiction-specific requirements.
Cannot confirm facts, sign agreements, or replace qualified legal counsel.

use_cases.title: Draft a Creator Partnership
use_cases.description: Build a clear agreement from agreed campaign terms, including payment, deliverables, approvals, disclosures, and usage rights.

use_cases.title: Review Agency Terms
use_cases.description: Identify missing protections, broad rights, payment risks, and negotiation points in an incoming agreement.

use_cases.title: Standardize Campaign Contracts
use_cases.description: Create a reusable template with consistent clauses and adjustable terms for different campaign sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Agreement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an influencer agreement for [creator] and [brand]. Include [deliverables], [compensation], [dates], owned-channel usage, FTC disclosure, and two revision rounds.

prompt_templates.title: Review Incoming Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this influencer agreement. List missing essential terms, red flags, the affected party, and suggested revisions: [paste agreement].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reusable Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable creator agreement for [campaign type]. Add selectable options for usage duration, exclusivity, whitelisting, payment schedules, approvals, and termination.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Negotiation Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these proposed terms with common ranges. Prioritize risks, propose fallback positions, and draft replacement language for each disputed clause: [paste terms].

output_examples.input: Draft a deal for two Instagram posts with a total fee of $500.
output_examples.output: A concise agreement covering two posts, payment timing, a publication schedule, limited owned-channel usage, FTC disclosure, revisions, termination, and signatures.

output_examples.input: Review a clause granting perpetual worldwide usage without additional payment.
output_examples.output: The review flags unlimited duration and scope, explains the creator impact, and proposes a paid license with defined channels and a fixed term.

output_examples.input: Prepare negotiation points for broad exclusivity and unlimited revisions.
output_examples.output: A prioritized negotiation sheet limits exclusivity by category and time, caps included revisions, and provides fallback positions for both terms.

best_practices: Provide exact party names, deliverables, dates, payment terms, platforms, and intended usage.
Mark unknown terms as pending instead of allowing assumptions to become contract language.
Have qualified counsel review the final agreement before anyone signs it.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated language as jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
Do not accept perpetual rights, broad exclusivity, or unlimited revisions without evaluating compensation and scope.
Do not store confidential rates or signed terms without approval and appropriate access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides general templates and review guidance. Qualified counsel should approve the final agreement.

faq.question: What agreements can it handle?
faq.answer: It supports influencer and creator partnerships involving content deliverables, compensation, usage rights, exclusivity, approvals, and disclosures.

faq.question: Can it review an existing contract?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the agreement text to receive missing-term checks, red flags, clause explanations, and negotiation suggestions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide party names, campaign details, deliverables, dates, fees, payment timing, platforms, usage needs, exclusivity, and approval rules.

faq.question: Does it adapt contracts to local law?
faq.answer: No. It includes placeholders for governing law and disputes, but it does not determine jurisdiction-specific enforceability.

faq.question: Can it sign or send the agreement?
faq.answer: It prepares agreement content. Signing or routing requires a configured e-signature service and separate user authorization.
